security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives from fenced examples and inline model IDs, but several examples intentionally run `infsh` or `npx` commands. The skill grants scoped Bash access to `infsh`, so prompts and image URLs may be sent to inference.sh or related providers. No prompt injection, obfuscation, credential theft, or arbitrary shell execution beyond the scoped CLI permission was found.

remediation.suggestion: State clearly that `infsh` commands send prompts and image URLs to external services, and ask before processing sensitive assets.
Keep the Bash permission limited to `infsh`, and document the intended subcommands for generation, listing, upscaling, and stitching.

remediation.issue: Remote image and install links in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Prefer marketplace-hosted images when possible, and mark `npx skills add` examples as manual user actions.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast access to image models without memorizing app IDs. This skill provides ready prompts and CLI patterns for generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching.
actual_capabilities: Lists image model app IDs for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
Shows inference.sh CLI patterns for text-to-image generation with prompt input.
Includes examples for image upscaling and stitching images from URL inputs.
Provides a discovery command for browsing image apps by category.
Links to inference.sh documentation for app execution and image generation workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI to be installed and authenticated before use.
Sends prompts, image URLs, and job metadata to external services.
Model availability, pricing, speed, and output quality are controlled by providers.
Provides command guidance; it does not generate images locally without inference.sh.

use_cases.title: Create Concept Art
use_cases.description: Generate initial visuals for scenes, characters, products, or environments using several image models.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Draft social graphics, poster concepts, and product mockups with repeatable prompt patterns.

use_cases.title: Prototype Image Workflows
use_cases.description: Test model app IDs, image upscaling, and stitching steps before adding them to automation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Product Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a studio product image prompt for a ceramic mug. Use the simplest recommended model and run it with inference.sh.

prompt_templates.title: Social Visual Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three image concepts for a summer launch campaign. Recommend models, aspect ratios, and concise prompts for each concept.

prompt_templates.title: Upscale Existing Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to upscale this image URL for ecommerce use: [image URL]. Explain what will be sent to the service first.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare FLUX, Gemini, and Seedream for a cinematic product concept. Run one generation per model, then summarize quality, speed, and text rendering.

output_examples.input: Product mockup for a stainless travel mug.
output_examples.output: A product-photo prompt, a recommended FLUX model, a square composition choice, and a follow-up upscaling step.

output_examples.input: Poster with clear text for an event announcement.
output_examples.output: A text-focused prompt, a Reve model recommendation, and guidance to inspect spelling before publishing.

output_examples.input: Two generated banner images that need one combined layout.
output_examples.output: A stitching workflow using image URLs, a horizontal layout recommendation, and a note about external image processing.

best_practices: Review prompts and image URLs for confidential information before running inference.sh commands.
Start with one model and one aspect ratio before comparing multiple providers.
Check generated text, brand details, and usage rights before publishing outputs.
anti_patterns: Do not send private customer images or unreleased product designs without approval.
Do not run related skill installation commands without verifying the source first.
Do not assume placeholder image URLs are safe production inputs.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI to run hosted image models.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The quick start includes an inference.sh login step before running models.

faq.question: Can it upscale images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a Topaz upscaler example that accepts an image URL.

faq.question: Can it compare image models?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists several model app IDs so users can run and compare outputs.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Prompts, image URLs, and job metadata may be sent to inference.sh or model providers.
